findings.highlight: striking Rider in the same motion
findings.evidenceJa: 返す刃で確実にライダーを“壊して”いく
findings.governingReading: With the returning blade, Saber certainly continues breaking Rider down.
findings.explanation: The English keeps the counterstrike but removes certainty, progressive destruction, and the marked language of “breaking” Rider.

findings.highlight: Natural healing that regenerates the wounds Saber sustains.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーによって傷つけられた体を癒す自然治癒
findings.governingReading: Rider spends resources on natural healing of the body Saber has wounded.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the wounds and their regeneration to Saber, reversing who is being injured and healed.

findings.evidenceJa: セイバーを抑えきれない
findings.governingReading: Rider must burn all fuel merely to keep Saber fully suppressed.
findings.explanation: The English changes a defensive containment requirement into general competitive equality.

findings.highlight: legs are starting to give in to the strain
findings.evidenceJa: 両脚は過度の酷使で、内部から崩壊しだしている
findings.governingReading: Both legs are beginning to collapse internally from extreme overuse.
findings.explanation: The English weakens internal structural collapse and excessive abuse into ordinary fatigue.

findings.highlight: It’s only a matter of time before Saber catches up to Rider’s speed.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーがライダーを捉えるのは時間の問題
findings.governingReading: It is only a matter of time before Saber catches Rider.
findings.explanation: The English invents Saber matching Rider’s speed, changing the predicted decisive capture into a speed comparison.

findings.highlight: The boy told Rider of his prediction
findings.evidenceJa: ライダーが少年に告げた戦いの結末
findings.governingReading: Before entering the cavern, Rider told the boy this exact outcome of the battle.
findings.explanation: The English directly reverses speaker and recipient, making Shirou the forecaster instead of Rider.

findings.evidenceJa: 泣きたくなるぐらい、理解できなくなっていく
findings.governingReading: Shirou is losing comprehension of visible things to a degree that makes him want to cry.
findings.explanation: The English preserves cognitive loss but removes its acute emotional degree.

findings.governingReading: The fragmented thought says only “I will lose,” before narrowing to something precious.
findings.explanation: The English supplies “everything,” expanding an intentionally objectless fear into total loss.

findings.highlight: I… have to do… what I can… and fight.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺は　　俺も　　自分にできる事で、たたか、
findings.governingReading: The broken thought catches between “I” and “I too” before failing during the word “fight.”
findings.explanation: The English smooths away the self-correction that aligns Shirou’s effort with Rider’s and completes more of the damaged syntax.

findings.evidenceJa: 彼女は命を預けると言った。
findings.governingReading: Shirou remembers that Rider said she would entrust her life to him.
findings.explanation: The English removes the explicit life-trust that makes his refusal to fail reciprocal rather than merely tactical.
